topic: Your degree plus 4 things: what your syllabus covers, what an internship interview checks, and how to add each one alongside college from first year
save_reason: A two-column cheat sheet: what your syllabus covers vs what an internship checks, with one thing to do for each gap (slide 7, full list in the caption).
send_reason: Send this to a friend who thinks marks alone will get the internship.

cover.concept: One surreal object: a black graduation cap on a white pedestal, its tassel ending in a small brass key.
hooks: Add these 4 things to your degree this year. (ambition)
What internships check that your syllabus skips. (curiosity)
Your degree plus one live project goes far. (awe)
Start the first of these 4 things tonight. (confidence)

slides.label: The difference
slides.idea: Not A or B, it's C: it's not marks or certificates, it's things you can show and explain (NYC_BRIEF: projects you can explain, problems you haven't seen).
slides.title: It's not your marks or your certificates.
slides.line: It's work you can show and explain in the interview.
slides.device: not A or B, it's C

slides.label: Thing 1
slides.idea: Practise problems you haven't seen: a few a week on a practice site, explain your approach out loud.
slides.title: Practise problems you haven't seen before.
slides.line: Solve three a week and explain your approach out loud.
slides.screen: A coding practice page cropped big: a fictional problem title and a 'Solved' tick list for this week, with a notes box 'My approach:' (.focus)

slides.label: Thing 2
slides.idea: Re-hook: here's a faster way to stand out: one project with a live link you can explain end to end.
slides.title: Here's a faster way: build one project people can open.
slides.line: Add a live link and explain how every part works.
slides.screen: A GitHub repo page cropped big: fictional repo aarav-codes/campus-bus with the About box showing a live link and a README section 'How it works: client, API, database' (.focus on the link)

slides.label: Thing 3
slides.idea: Work with people who build: a hackathon or an open-source team, where you learn Git with others.
slides.title: Build with a team at a hackathon.
slides.line: You learn Git, deadlines and teamwork in one weekend.

slides.label: Thing 4
slides.idea: This won't work unless you can check AI's code: use AI, then find what it got wrong (NYC_BRIEF core belief).
slides.title: This won't work unless you can check AI's code.
slides.line: Read every change it makes and test it yourself.
slides.screen: A code review diff cropped big: a fictional AI suggestion with one wrong line marked and a review comment 'This breaks when the list is empty' (.focus)
